comments.body:
How is this?

| # | Description | Level | #v5.0.be |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: |
| **3.4.4** | Verify that all responses contain a X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff header field to prevent MIME type sniffing vulnerabilities. | 2 | v5.0.be-50.3.2 |

There some obscure reasons - especially around uploaded content - that still makes this a little important in modern browsers.

I have it assigned to myself.

There are some other reasons as well.

Documenting source info:
* https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#x-content-type-options-header
* https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/master/services/network/cross_origin_read_blocking_explainer.md
* https://www.chromium.org/Home/chromium-security/corb-for-developers/
* https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/X-Content-Type-Options
@ryarmst are you familiar with any context here or do you think you could go through these links to make a proposal?
Just leaving a note: it is a low-priority task because a valid requirement exists, but it can just be improved with "self-explanatory text" on why it exists.

The key points to use:
* disables mime type sniffing
* requires correct/expected content-type from destination resource
* enables browsers Cross-Origin Read Blocking (CORB)

Proposal attempt:
> Verify that all responses contain an 'X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff' header field to instruct browsers not to use content sniffing for the given response, require a correct Content-Type header field value from the destination resource (such as a resource for style is accepted only with text/css), and enable Cross-Origin Read Blocking (CORB).

> require a correct Content-Type header field value from the destination resource (such as a resource for style is accepted only with text/css),

I don't really understand what is intended here, neither how to implement nor how to test.

> enable Cross-Origin Read Blocking (CORB)

I can see that CORB relies on the Content-Type and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff headers but it isn't directly related, are you sure they should be in the same requirement? Seems like one is solving the problem of content being misinterpreted and the other is preventing side-channel leakage

> > require a correct Content-Type header field value from the destination resource (such as a resource for style is accepted only with text/css),
> 
> I don't really understand what is intended here, neither how to implement nor how to test.

There is nothing more to implement than adding the mentioned header.

> > enable Cross-Origin Read Blocking (CORB)
> 
> I can see that CORB relies on the Content-Type and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff headers but it isn't directly related, are you sure they should be in the same requirement? Seems like one is solving the problem of content being misinterpreted and the other is preventing side-channel leakage

It is the explanation why the requirement header is requirement exists.

> > > require a correct Content-Type header field value from the destination resource (such as a resource for style is accepted only with text/css),
> > 
> > 
> > I don't really understand what is intended here, neither how to implement nor how to test.
> 
> There is nothing more to implement than adding the mentioned header.

But saying "such as a resource for style is accepted only with text/css" seems to indicate that we need to be checking something or ensuring something other than just adding the nosniff header. Is the intention just to say, "make sure the Content-Type of the response matches the type of the content in the response.
 
> > > enable Cross-Origin Read Blocking (CORB)
> > 
> > 
> > I can see that CORB relies on the Content-Type and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff headers but it isn't directly related, are you sure they should be in the same requirement? Seems like one is solving the problem of content being misinterpreted and the other is preventing side-channel leakage
> 
> It is the explanation why the requirement header is requirement exists.

Is preventing content sniffing not a goal in itself?

> But saying "such as a resource for style is accepted only with text/css" seems to indicate that we need to be checking something or ensuring something other than just adding the nosniff header. Is the intention just to say, "make sure the Content-Type of the response matches the type of the content in the response.

No, by providing the header we require browser to check that.

> Is preventing content sniffing not a goal in itself?

Preventing content sniffing is just one goal to achieve with that.

I think it makes sense to read materials provided here: https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/2870#issuecomment-2776759177

I think this is a great direction. Small suggestions:

_Verify that all HTTP responses include the X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff header to prevent content and MIME type and sniffing, require that resources declare a correct and expected Content-Type header (e.g., stylesheets must use text/css), and ensure that Cross-Origin Read Blocking (CORB) is enabled._

> to prevent content and MIME type and sniffing

There is something weird. Maybe "to prevent content sniffing and MIME type guessing"?

Attempt to be more precise with wording to say out, that it instructs browser to do those activities:
> Verify that all HTTP responses contain an 'X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff' header field. This instructs browsers not to use content sniffing and MIME type guessing for the given response, instructs to require a correct Content-Type header field value from the destination resource (such as a resource for style is accepted only with text/css), and enables Cross-Origin Read Blocking (CORB).

I hear you. The three terms I see are MIME sniffing, content sniffing or media type sniffing. I think mime-sniffing is the most popular. So maybe one more re-organization works for you:

_Verify that all HTTP responses include the X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff header to prevent MIME sniffing and ensure that Cross-Origin Read Blocking (CORB) is enabled. Also require that resources declare a correct and expected Content-Type header (e.g., stylesheets must use text/css)._

In general, I really like the direction you are proposing here @elarlang and am just trying to do a little word smithing.

Ah, I just hit send the same time as you. I'm pretty flexible. But I think it reads a little better of the content-type part is at the end.

My suggestions are in, but please feel free to make the final call here.

So I really struggled with this and I think @elarlang's suggestion made things a lot clearer to me, even though it is a little wordier. The think about request destinations is really subtle and not something  I was aware of.

Some subtle changes:

_"Verify that all HTTP responses contain an 'X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff' header field. This instructs browsers not to use content sniffing and MIME type guessing for the given response, and to require the response's Content-Type header field value to match the destination resource. For example, the response to a request for a style is only accepted if the response's Content-Type is 'text/css'. This also enables the use of the Cross-Origin Read Blocking (CORB) header field which the response should also contain._"

> This also enables the use of the Cross-Origin Read Blocking (CORB) header field which the response should also contain.

This is not a header field, it's a browser's feature.

Just update to my previous proposal to explain the point:
> Verify that all HTTP responses contain an 'X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff' header field. This instructs browsers not to use content sniffing and MIME type guessing for the given response, instructs to require a correct Content-Type header field value from the destination resource (such as a resource for style is accepted only with text/css), and **enables browsers' Cross-Origin Read Blocking (CORB) functionality**.
